framework: AWS Security Best Practices + HackTricks Cloud AWS
description: SQS/SNS policies, injection, and exfiltration persistence checks

items.title: SQS queue policy uses aws:PrincipalOrgID backdoor-style access
items.description: Org-scoped access via aws:PrincipalOrgID can create hidden broad access paths.
items.remediation: Review SQS queue policies and restrict principals explicitly; avoid org-wide broad permissions unless required.

pci_dss.reason: Least privilege for access to sensitive systems and data flows.

items.title: SQS redrive configuration could enable DLQ-based exfiltration
items.description: DLQ/RedrivePolicy and RedriveAllowPolicy can be abused to siphon messages to attacker-controlled queues.
items.remediation: Lock down who can modify queue attributes; review DLQ targets and allow policies; enforce KMS and tight key policies.

pci_dss.reason: Monitoring of changes and access to messaging systems helps detect exfiltration paths.

items.title: SNS to SQS injection risk via permissive queue/topic policies
items.description: Permissive SNS/SQS policies can allow untrusted publishers to inject messages into trusted queues.
items.remediation: Restrict queue policies to specific SNS topic ARNs with aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount conditions.

pci_dss.reason: Permissive SNS/SQS policies that allow wildcard or untrusted sources violate least-privilege access control. PCI DSS 7.2.1 requires access to systems be restricted based on business need-to-know.

items.title: Unmonitored message move tasks could enable DLQ data theft
items.description: DLQ message move operations can rapidly exfiltrate accumulated messages if abused.
items.remediation: Restrict SQS administrative permissions; monitor CloudTrail for message move operations; encrypt DLQs with KMS.

pci_dss.reason: Time-synchronized audit logging and monitoring support detection of abnormal administrative actions.

items.title: SQS queue policy allows wildcard principal for data-plane operations
items.description: SQS policies granting Send/Receive/Delete/ChangeVisibility to wildcard principals expose queues to unauthorized injection, theft, and disruption.
items.remediation: Restrict queue policy principals explicitly and require strong conditions (SourceArn/SourceAccount) for service-to-service paths.

pci_dss.reason: Messaging resources carrying sensitive workflows must enforce strict least-privilege access.

items.title: SQS queue without encryption at rest
items.description: Queues without KMS-managed or SQS-managed server-side encryption increase risk of message disclosure at rest.
items.remediation: Enable SSE using KMS CMKs for sensitive queues (or SQS managed SSE where acceptable) and validate key policy constraints.

pci_dss.reason: Sensitive data at rest must be protected with strong cryptography and key management controls.

items.title: SNS topic policy allows wildcard/external Subscribe
items.description: Permissive sns:Subscribe grants enable unauthorized subscriptions and message exfiltration channels.
items.remediation: Allow subscriptions only from approved principals/endpoints and remove wildcard subscribe permissions.

pci_dss.reason: Message fanout channels must enforce explicit authorization to prevent data leakage.

items.title: SNS topic policy allows unrestricted wildcard Publish
items.description: Broad sns:Publish permissions can enable unauthorized message injection and abuse of downstream integrations.
items.remediation: Restrict publishing principals and enforce source conditions for trusted service integrations.

pci_dss.reason: Permissive SNS/SQS policies that allow wildcard or untrusted sources violate least-privilege access control. PCI DSS 7.2.1 requires access to systems be restricted based on business need-to-know.

items.title: SNS topic policy grants administrative actions to wildcard principal
items.description: Wildcard principals with administrative SNS actions (DeleteTopic, SetTopicAttributes, AddPermission, RemovePermission) can modify or destroy the topic and its subscriptions.
items.remediation: Remove administrative actions from resource policies; restrict to specific IAM principals using conditions. Prefer IAM identity policies over resource policies for administrative operations.

pci_dss.reason: Administrative access to messaging infrastructure must be restricted to authorized principals only.

notes: Messaging is region-scoped. Findings should include evidence_refs into queue/topic attributes and policies.
